subject: EdenLoop capacity placement plan & safety buffer runbook
messages:
From: Sara Khanna <sara.khanna@edenloop.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@edenloop.ai
Date: Wed, 24 Oct 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for Q1 launch (high priority)

Hi Laura,

Quick note — EdenLoop is planning an early Q1 launch for our generative search product. Procurement asked me to reach out with expected inference demand so we can lock capacity. High-level ask: we expect a cold-start weekly average of ~22M tokens/day with 95th p99 concurrency spikes equivalent to ~60 concurrent A100-xl pods for short bursts.

Goal: dedicated pool that gives predictable latency during launch week, plus a safety buffer while we finalize the contract (2-4 weeks). Can your team run an availability check and give a sizing + placement recommendation?

Attachments: I attached a small demand snapshot (edenloop_demand_snapshot.xlsx) showing forecasted usage and ramp assumptions.

We are on a tight timeline — would appreciate an initial read by EOD Thursday if possible.

Thanks,
Sara Khanna
Head of Platform Partnerships
EdenLoop

---
From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.khanna@edenloop.ai
Date: Wed, 24 Oct 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity sizing for Q1 launch (high priority)

Sara — thanks for the snapshot and the timeline. Mateo / Ben — looping you in to do a quick feasibility + provisional hold assessment.

Ask for infra check (Mateo):
- Feasible to meet ~60 A100-xl concurrent spike for 48–72 hour windows?
- Recommend dedicated pool size for consistent latency at 95th percentile given their forecast (attached).
- Suggested safety buffer (expressed in A100-equivalent nodes) for a 2–4 week soft-hold before contract signature.

Ben — if infra confirms feasible, can you prepare a short mutual action plan and note whether we should request a provisional capacity hold (soft-hold) tied to HubSpot deal DL-2028-089? We want to avoid double-booking in our fleet during the Q1 ramp.

I copied Sara so EdenLoop sees we moved this immediately. Mateo — appreciate an initial note by Thursday EOD PST.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
From: mateo.alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.khanna@edenloop.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Oct 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity sizing for Q1 launch (high priority)

Laura / Ben — quick infra read below (initial, non-binding). I pulled last 90-day utilization and current reservation schedule across our US pools. See attached capacity_calc_v1.pdf for the math.

Summary (short):
- Baseline: supporting 60 A100-xl concurrent spikes (sustained 5–12 minutes) requires ~48 physical A100-xl nodes if we rely on conservative packing and per-request KV cache needs.
- Dedicated pool recommendation: provision a dedicated pool of 56 A100-xl-equivalent nodes (this gives ~15% safety buffer for minor forecast error and preserves headroom for small bursts).
- Alternative mixed-variant option: 40 A100-xl + 32 q4-quantized L40x nodes behind a cost-aware routing policy for non-critical inference — reduces unit cost but introduces small variance in p99 latency.
- Availability window: based on current reservations and planned expansions, we can offer a provisional soft-hold for up to 45 nodes immediately for a 3-week window. Full 56-node commitment requires shift of two planned maintenance allocations and would need a signed commitment within 10 business days to guarantee.

Operational notes:
- Placement: prefer us-west-2 pool A (lower network egress) for the dedicated nodes; fallback us-east-1 pool B if capacity in west saturates.
- KV cache warm-up: recommend a pre-warm plan 48 hrs ahead of launch; we can surface warm-up tooling to EdenLoop.
- Cost delta: mixed-variant option reduces expected token unit cost by ~18% at the expense of p99 latency jitter.

Attachments: capacity_calc_v1.pdf (capacity table + assumptions).

If Ben wants a short paragraph we can include as part of a mutual action plan and request a soft-hold ticket. Mateo

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.khanna@edenloop.ai, procurement@edenloop.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Oct 2028 11:01:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity sizing for Q1 launch (high priority)

Thanks Mateo — that’s helpful and pragmatic. Laura, I drafted a short mutual action plan and a request for a provisional capacity soft-hold tied to HubSpot DL-2028-089. I attached MAP v3 (mutual_action_plan_v3.docx).

Key points I added to the MAP:
- Redwood to provision soft-hold for 45 A100-equivalent nodes in us-west-2 pool A for 3 weeks pending signed PO.
- EdenLoop to provide finalized PO and DS signature within 10 business days to firm the pool to 56 nodes (per Mateo).
- Shared responsibility: Redwood operations will run pre-warm script; EdenLoop will provide representative warm-up prompts.

DocuSign link (provisional): https://www.docusign.com/link/edn-DL-2028-089

Action: Laura — can you authorize me to open a provisional capacity ticket with Ops? I’ll include the MAP and capacity_calc_v1.pdf. Ops will mark the ticket as "soft-hold" and tag the nodes — non-binding until contract execution.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
